title: Editing, undo and copy
summary: Edit a cell, cancel your typing and clear content, then undo, redo, copy and paste from the keyboard.
intro:
The shortcuts you will use most in Excel are the editing ones: getting into a cell to change it, cancelling what you typed, undoing a mistake, and copying and pasting.

Copy, paste and undo work the same way in most programs, so what you learn here you can use everywhere.

faq.q: What is the difference between Delete and Esc?
faq.a: Delete clears the content of the selected cell. Esc cancels what you are typing before you confirm it, so the cell stays as it was.

faq.q: How many steps can I undo?
faq.a: Excel usually keeps your last hundred actions, so you can press Ctrl+Z several times. Some actions, such as saving and closing the file, clear that history.

edit-a-cell.prompt: To edit the selected cell without erasing it, press `F2`; the cursor appears at the end of the text. On Mac the shortcut is `Ctrl+U`.
edit-a-cell.hint: The second key in the row of F keys at the top of the keyboard.

cancel-typing.prompt: You started typing in a cell, then changed your mind before confirming. Press `Esc` to cancel and put the cell back as it was.

clear-a-cell.prompt: To clear the content of the selected cell, press `Delete`. On a Mac, press the key labelled delete.

undo.prompt: You cleared the wrong cell! Press `Ctrl+Z` (on Mac: `⌘+Z`) to undo your last action.
undo.hint: Z is the key next to the left Shift.

redo.prompt: You undid one step too many. To redo it, press `Ctrl+Y` (on Mac: `⌘+Y`).

copy.prompt: To copy the selected cells, press `Ctrl+C` (on Mac: `⌘+C`). A moving border stays around them until you paste.

paste.prompt: Select the destination cell, then press `Ctrl+V` (on Mac: `⌘+V`) to paste what you copied.
